outcome: time from skin incision to delivery
cohort: 298 women with a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 50 kg/m(2) and a cesarean birth with documented skin incision type
finding: In superobese women, vertical skin incision was not associated with increased wound complications, but was associated with an increased risk for classical hysterotomy.
mod_finding: Vertical skin incision was not associated with a higher risk for composite wound morbidity after adjusting for covariates, but was significantly associated with classical hysterotomy without an associated decrease in incision to delivery time or neonatal morbidity.
